name: list_layers
description: List all available raster layers with their indicator name, year, season, description, and access tier. Use this to discover what data is available before analyzing an area.

name: get_legend
description: Get the legend (value → label mapping) for a specific indicator. This tells you what each pixel value means (e.g., 0 = Not eligible, 2 = Eligible). Essential for interpreting analysis results.

name: analyze_area
description: Analyze a raster layer within a given Area of Interest (AOI). For categorical layers: returns pixel counts per category. For continuous layers: returns min, max, mean, median, std. The AOI must be a GeoJSON geometry (Polygon or MultiPolygon).

name: get_layer_bounds
description: Get the geographic bounding box of a layer in WGS84 coordinates. Useful to know the spatial extent of a dataset.

name: lookup_province
description: Look up a Spanish province by name and get its geographic boundary. Returns the province name, code, and bounding box. Use this when the user mentions a province name (e.g., 'Murcia', 'Barcelona', 'Sevilla'). After calling this tool, call analyze_area with an empty {} for the aoi parameter — the system will inject the province geometry automatically.

name: lookup_municipality
description: Look up a Spanish municipality (municipio) by name and get its geographic boundary. Returns the municipality name, code, province, CCAA, and bounding box. Use this when the user mentions a specific town or city (e.g., 'Villanueva de la Serena', 'Lorca', 'Getafe'). Optionally provide a province hint to disambiguate. After calling this tool, call analyze_area with an empty {} for the aoi parameter — the system will inject the municipality geometry automatically.

name.description: Municipality name in Spanish (e.g., 'Villanueva de la Serena', 'Lorca')

name: compare_areas
description: Compare two Spanish provinces side-by-side on a single indicator. Returns statistics for both areas and a one-line comparison note. REQUIRED for any province comparison question — call once per pair. For three provinces, call this twice (e.g., A vs B, then A vs C).

name: find_top_n
description: Find the top or bottom N Spanish provinces by a metric using pre-computed rankings. Instant — no raster reads needed. Use this for ranking questions ('which province has the highest CO2 eligibility?', 'top 10 erosion risk provinces'). Optionally scope results to specific provinces with filter_provinces.

order.description: 'desc' for top (highest first), 'asc' for bottom (lowest first). Default: 'desc'

filter_provinces.description: Optional list of province names to restrict results to (e.g., ['Murcia', 'Córdoba', 'Jaén'])

name: generate_chart
description: Create a PNG chart from data and upload it to GCS. Returns the GCS URI. Use this after any comparison or ranking analysis to produce a visual output. chart_type options: 'stacked_bar' (CO2 class breakdown per province), 'ranked_bar' (horizontal ranking), 'grouped_bar' (multi-metric side-by-side), 'bar' (simple bar).

data.description: Array of data objects. Each must have a 'label' key. For stacked_bar: other keys are stack segments (e.g., {label: 'Murcia', Eligible: 68.2, Conditional: 18.1}). For ranked_bar: {label: 'Ciudad Real', value: 78.9}. For grouped_bar: same as stacked_bar but rendered side-by-side.

output_prefix.description: GCS path prefix under the bucket (e.g., 'poc/experiments/exp_poc_001/visualizations')

filename.description: Filename without extension (auto-generated from title if omitted)

name: analyze_multi_layer
description: Analyze multiple indicators for the same province in one call. More efficient than separate analyze_area calls — runs raster reads in parallel. Use this for combined multi-indicator analysis (e.g., CO2 eligibility + erosion risk together for a province deep-dive).

indicators.description: List of indicators to analyze. Each item: {indicator, year, season}

name: toggle_layer
description: Toggle a map layer on or off. Use this when the user asks to show, display, hide, or remove a dataset on the map. Available layers: co2_spain_legislation, rf_gully_probability, ines_erosion_potencial, ines_movimientos_masa, ines_erosion_eolica, mfe, burnt_areas, lucas_gully_channels, lucas_gully_locations, lucas_survey_points, lucas_crosscheck_random, lucas_crosscheck_omission.

visible.description: True to show the layer, false to hide it

name: query_erosion_stats
description: Query pre-computed spectral index statistics for Murcia municipalities (2018-2025). Supports timeseries (monthly values for one municipality), ranking (municipalities sorted by index value), and seasonal (average monthly pattern). Available indices: ndvi (vegetation), bsi (bare soil / erosion proxy), ndwi (water), ndbi (built-up), msi (moisture stress), savi (soil-adjusted vegetation), nbr (burn ratio), fvc (fractional vegetation cover). Use this for erosion analysis, vegetation trends, fire recovery, and seasonal pattern questions about Murcia.

query_type.description: Query type: 'timeseries' (monthly values for a municipality), 'ranking' (municipalities sorted by index), 'seasonal' (average monthly pattern)

municipality.description: Municipality name (required for timeseries, optional for seasonal). E.g., 'Lorca', 'Cartagena', 'Murcia'

name: create_buffer
description: Create a buffer zone around a province or municipality geometry. Returns a GeoJSON polygon representing the buffered area. Useful for proximity queries like 'what municipalities are within 50 km of Murcia?' — first buffer the source area, then use select_features_by_spatial_relationship to find intersecting features.

province_hint.description: Optional province name to disambiguate municipalities

name: select_features_by_spatial_relationship
description: Select provinces or municipalities that satisfy a spatial relationship with a reference area. Spatial predicates: 'intersects', 'within', 'contains', 'touches', 'overlaps'. Uses OR logic — features matching ANY predicate are returned. Useful after create_buffer to find nearby areas, or to find all municipalities within a province.

reference_area.description: Name of the reference province or municipality

target_type.description: Type of features to select: 'provinces' or 'municipalities'

reference_aoi.description: Optional GeoJSON geometry to use as reference instead of looking up by name (e.g., a buffered geometry from create_buffer)

province_hint.description: Optional province name to disambiguate reference municipality

name: get_centroids
description: Get the geographic centroid (center point) of one or more provinces or municipalities. Returns centroid coordinates (lat/lon) for each area. Useful for distance calculations or point-based spatial queries.

area_names.description: List of province or municipality names

province_hint.description: Optional province name to disambiguate municipalities

name: reject_task
description: Call this tool when the user's question cannot be answered with the available tools and data. This prevents hallucinating an answer. Use when: the question requires data you don't have, asks about areas outside Spain, or needs analysis capabilities not available in the current toolset.

reason.description: Brief explanation of why the task cannot be completed
